evidence_against: BTC and ETH spot prices moved in opposite directions: BTCUSDT close fell 0.2286% while ETHUSDT rose 0.4126%.
ETHBTC improved 0.6460%, from 0.02941 to 0.02960, which contradicts a broad risk-off or weakening-ETH transmission signal.
Funding declined for both BTC and ETH swaps, reducing the observed funding-stress signal; BTC funding fell 13.0% and ETH funding fell 26.7%.
The current capture does not provide BTC dominance, total2/total3, stablecoin dominance, ETF flows, or CFGI components, so rotation and sentiment hypotheses cannot be fully evaluated.
Observed spot ranges and volumes contracted substantially versus the predecessor, including BTC volume down 41.7% and ETH volume down 89.2%, limiting directional interpretation.
evidence_for: Breadth deteriorated: decliners increased from 54 to 58 and flat constituents fell from 21 to 17, while advancers remained at 25.
BTCUSDT close declined 0.2286% and OKX BTC mark price declined 0.2579% against the predecessor.
BTC open interest rose 0.9555% while BTC price declined, a partial leverage-price divergence consistent with the leverage-stress component of the pullback hypotheses.
ETH open interest also increased 0.7097%, despite the mixed spot and relative-performance signals.
The observed breadth deterioration plus BTC price weakness partially matches the live sensors for LKO-PULLBACK-001 and LKO-PULLBACK-002, but the match is incomplete and unratified.

forecast_candidates.rationale: The latest BTC observation is confined to a narrow 0.1195% intraperiod range, with only a modest predecessor decline and reduced volume. This supports a short-horizon range candidate rather than a strong directional candidate.

Breadth deterioration is the clearest current directional signal: decliners increased from 54 to 58 and flat constituents decreased from 21 to 17. This is a monitoring candidate for continued breadth weakening, not a canonical forecast.

ETHBTC improved versus the predecessor but remained within a very narrow latest interval, so the available evidence supports relative-performance stability or consolidation rather than a validated rotation breakout.

hypotheses: LKO-PULLBACK-001: PARTIALLY MATCHED. LKO-PULLBACK-002: PARTIALLY MATCHED. BTC weakened, breadth deteriorated, and open interest increased, but ETH strengthened and ETHBTC improved while funding declined. The rapid-advance prerequisite is not established by the supplied deltas.

LKO-ROTATION-002: CANNOT FULLY EVALUATE. Breadth and ETHBTC are available, but BTC dominance, total3, and complete funding/open-interest change context are not supplied for the full hypothesis.

summary: Current evidence shows a mixed configuration: breadth weakened and BTC price declined while open interest rose, but funding eased and ETH relative performance improved. Pullback hypotheses receive only partial support; rotation, CFGI, and broader transmission hypotheses remain incomplete because required sensors are missing. Forecast candidates are shadow-only and unratified.
